name: Tulsi (Holy Basil)
uses: Traditionally used for coughs, colds, sore throat and to support immunity. Also used as a calming herb for everyday stress.
how_to_take: Fresh leaves chewed or boiled in water as tea (kadha), often with ginger and honey.
caution: May lower blood sugar and can thin blood slightly. Avoid large amounts in pregnancy and around surgery.

name: Turmeric
uses: Used for inflammation, joint stiffness and minor wounds. Curcumin is the active compound studied most.
how_to_take: Half a teaspoon in warm milk or food with black pepper, which helps absorption.
caution: High doses or supplements can upset the stomach and may interact with blood thinners. Use caution with gallstones.

name: Ginger
uses: Used for nausea, motion sickness, indigestion and bloating, and to ease cold symptoms.
how_to_take: Fresh slices steeped in hot water, or a small piece chewed before meals.
caution: Large amounts can cause heartburn. May add to the effect of blood thinners and diabetes medicines.

name: Ashwagandha
uses: An adaptogen traditionally used for stress, poor sleep and tiredness.
how_to_take: Powder (about 1/2 teaspoon) in warm milk at night, or standardized capsules as labelled.
caution: Avoid in pregnancy. Can affect thyroid, blood sugar and sedative medicines. Not for people with autoimmune conditions without medical advice.

name: Neem
uses: Used externally for acne, itching and scalp problems, and traditionally as a blood purifier.
how_to_take: Leaf paste on the skin, neem water for washing, or neem twig for teeth.
caution: Do not give to infants or children internally. Avoid in pregnancy and when trying to conceive.

name: Aloe Vera
uses: The gel soothes minor burns, sunburn and dry skin. Juice is traditionally used for acidity.
how_to_take: Apply fresh gel directly to the skin. Drink only products labelled as purified for drinking.
caution: Aloe latex (yellow sap) is a strong laxative and unsafe in pregnancy. Patch test the gel first.

name: Giloy (Guduchi)
uses: Traditionally used to support immunity and recover from recurring fevers.
how_to_take: Stem decoction or standardized tablets, usually for short periods.
caution: Can lower blood sugar and stimulate the immune system. Avoid with autoimmune disease, around surgery, and in pregnancy. Reports link it to liver injury in some people.

name: Brahmi
uses: Traditionally used to support memory, focus and calm, popular with students.
how_to_take: Standardized capsules or powder with ghee or milk. Effects build over weeks, not hours.
caution: Can cause stomach upset and slow the heart rate. Use caution with thyroid or sedative medicines.

name: Amla (Indian Gooseberry)
uses: Very rich in vitamin C. Used for immunity, digestion, hair health and general rejuvenation.
how_to_take: Fresh fruit, juice, or a teaspoon of powder in water.
caution: May lower blood sugar and slow clotting. Take care before surgery and with diabetes medicines.

name: Fenugreek (Methi)
uses: Used to support blood sugar control, digestion and breast milk supply.
how_to_take: Soak a teaspoon of seeds overnight and drink the water, or add seeds to food.
caution: Can drop blood sugar too far with diabetes medicines. Avoid large amounts in pregnancy.

name: Peppermint
uses: Used for gas, bloating, irritable bowel symptoms and tension headaches.
how_to_take: Tea from fresh or dried leaves after meals.
caution: Can worsen acid reflux. Do not apply peppermint oil to the face of young children.

name: Chamomile
uses: A gentle herb for relaxation, mild sleep trouble and stomach cramps.
how_to_take: A cup of tea in the evening, steeped for 5 to 10 minutes.
caution: People allergic to ragweed or daisies may react. May add to the effect of blood thinners.

name: Garlic
uses: Used to support heart health and cholesterol, and traditionally for colds.
how_to_take: One or two raw or lightly crushed cloves with food.
caution: Raises bleeding risk with blood thinners and before surgery. Can irritate the stomach.

name: Cinnamon
uses: Used in cooking and tea for digestion and to support healthy blood sugar.
how_to_take: A small pinch to half a teaspoon in tea, oats or food.
caution: Cassia type has coumarin, which can harm the liver in large amounts. Keep to small daily amounts.

name: Mulethi (Licorice Root)
uses: A classic throat soother used for dry cough, sore throat and hoarse voice.
how_to_take: A small piece of root chewed slowly, or steeped in hot water as tea for a few days.
caution: Long use or large amounts can raise blood pressure and lower potassium. Avoid in pregnancy, heart disease and high blood pressure.

name: Lavender
uses: Used for tension headaches, stress and light sleep. Often used as aroma or tea.
how_to_take: Inhale the aroma of the flowers or oil, or drink as a mild tea. Dilute oil before it touches skin.
caution: Do not swallow the essential oil. It may cause drowsiness with sedatives. Skin reactions are possible.
